The [YAML to JSON Converter](/yaml-to-json) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert YAML to JSON — paste YAML, get valid JSON back. Enter your YAML input and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Convert YAML into JSON: paste YAML in, get pretty-printed JSON out. YAML is the format used for configuration files, CI pipelines and data exchange, and JSON is what most APIs and JavaScript code expect — this tool bridges the two. It handles nested maps, lists, quoted strings, numbers, booleans and nulls. If the YAML has a syntax error, the tool shows the error with its line number instead of guessing. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the YAML to JSON Converter

Start by typing or pasting your YAML input. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste your YAML into the input box.
2. Read the JSON output — it is pretty-printed with two-space indentation.
3. If there is an error, read the message, fix the line it points to, and try again.

## How it works

The [YAML to JSON Converter](/yaml-to-json) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. “name: CalcHub, version: 2, features: calculators, blog” becomes {"name": "CalcHub", "version": 2, "features": ["calculators", "blog"]}. Try the same figures in the [YAML to JSON Converter](/yaml-to-json) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (YAML input: name: CalcHub version: 2 features: - calculators - blog - admin settings: theme: light analytics: true), the [YAML to JSON Converter](/yaml-to-json) returns JSON output: { "name": "CalcHub", "version": 2, "features": [ "calculators", "blog", "admin" ], "settings": { "theme": "light", "analytics": true } }, Status: Valid YAML. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. ## YAML basics

YAML uses indentation to show structure: two spaces per level, never tabs. key: value makes a mapping, - item makes a list item, and # starts a comment. Strings usually need no quotes, but quote them if they contain a colon, a # or leading/trailing spaces. Numbers, true/false and null are read as their types, not as strings — so version: 2 becomes the number 2 in JSON, not "2".

## Common YAML errors

The two errors that catch almost everyone are tabs (YAML forbids them — use spaces) and inconsistent indentation (a child line must be indented further than its parent, by the same amount throughout). A colon inside an unquoted string also breaks parsing — “time: 10:30” needs quotes around the value. The error message names the line and column, which is usually enough to find the problem.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Use spaces, never tabs — YAML forbids tab indentation.
- Keep one indentation width (usually two spaces) through the whole file.
- Quote strings that contain a colon, a # or special characters.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is YAML used for?

Mostly configuration: Docker Compose files, GitHub Actions workflows, Kubernetes manifests, and application settings. It is easier for humans to read than JSON, while JSON is easier for programs to parse — hence converting between them. Try it with your own numbers in the [YAML to JSON Converter](/yaml-to-json) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does my YAML fail to parse?

Almost always tabs or inconsistent indentation. YAML requires spaces and a consistent indent width. A colon inside an unquoted value is the next most common cause — quote the value. Try it with your own numbers in the [YAML to JSON Converter](/yaml-to-json) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does this support anchors and multi-line strings?

Yes — the converter uses a full YAML parser, so anchors (&a), aliases (*a), and block scalars (| and >) all work, not just simple key-value pairs. Try it with your own numbers in the [YAML to JSON Converter](/yaml-to-json) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
